ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, Sept. 3, 2001, as amended); Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 5493, Dec. 31, 1997, as amended); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 6515, Sept. 3, 2001, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, Dec. 3, 1962, as amended); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, Sept. 16, 1998, as amended); and the relevant Financial Services Commission/Korea Financial Intelligence Unit enforcement decrees, Beneficial Ownership examination standards, and customer due diligence guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (registered extract) of each foreign shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Corporate Agency in the jurisdiction of origin of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is a Hague Apostille Convention member other than Korea: notarize the document, obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority of that state, and submit a certified Korean translation; no consular legalization is to be added. If the issuing state is a non-member: notarize, authenticate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, then legalize at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in the issuing state. The Apostille and consular legalization tracks are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry / Tax Authority in the jurisdiction of origin of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notarize and issue an Apostille in the issuing state, then deliver an officially licensed Korean translation. Non-Hague route: notarize, authenticate at the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and obtain Korean consular legalization at the Korean Mission. Because these are alternative procedures, an instrument bearing an Apostille must not subsequently be submitted for consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean Yuhan Hoesa incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent or ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the resolution before a notary public in the issuing state. For Hague member states, attach an Apostille issued by the competent authority of the issuing state. For non-Hague states, attach Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate. The two routes are parallel and exclusive; do not chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association of the foreign shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or official custodian of corporate records in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize a certified copy. In Hague member states, affix an Apostille in the state of issuance and provide a certified Korean translation. In non-Hague states, have the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state authenticate the notarized copy, then have the Korean Embassy/Consulate legalize it. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the financial history, conduct, and responsibility of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depository bank in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer's signature must be notarized. For a bank located in a Hague member state, obtain an Apostille in that state and submit a certified Korean translation. For a bank in a non-Hague state, authenticate the notarized letter at the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalize it at the Korean Embassy/Consulate. Never use Apostille and consular legalization on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certificate. If the issuing state is a Hague member state, the only authentication required is an Apostille. If the issuing state is not a Hague member, require Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate. The two authentication regimes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and counterparty banks against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HMT sanctions, Korean government sanctions lists, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists. Any person classed as a foreign PEP, domestic PEP, subject of targeted financial sanctions, or adverse media hit requires senior management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, documented source of wealth and source of funds, and a written risk justification before a bank account is opened or a corporate action proceeds. The same protocol applies to every beneficial owner holding 25 percent or more of the Yuhan Hoesa. Each screening hit must be reviewed within one Korean business day and logged in the AML/CFT audit trail.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Registry Office / Korea Internet Registration Office (i-REGISTRO) commercial registration name search, together with the National Tax Service business registration name check; the official automated clearance is the court registry name availability search.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Yuhan Hoesa trade name must be expressed in the Hangul script and must contain a distinctive element, the legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa, and no identical or misleadingly similar match with an existing Korean commercial name. A foreign-language parallel name may be used for branding but is not a substitute for the registered Korean name. The four-tier naming convention requires: (i) exact Hangul match; (ii) phonetically identical transliteration of a foreign word; (iii) partially descriptive term plus a distinctive identifier; and (iv) a foreign-language name transliterated into Hangul. Foreign word marks must be transliterated into Hangul, and evidence of trademark registration may be requested where the trade name is not in Korean characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are not extendable under current Korean court registry practice; after the 30-day window expires, the applicant may file a new reservation for the same name if it remains clear. If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant has 30 days from rejection to file a written administrative appeal with the head of the local Supreme Court Registry Office, stating the statutory basis for distinctiveness, non-conflict, and compliance with the Commercial Act. The registry must re-examine the application through the same clearance algorithms. If the rejection is affirmed, counsel may file an immediate appeal to the relevant district court or commence administrative adjudication under the Administrative Litigation Act. As a practical measure, at least three alternative names should be submitted at initial filing to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is strongly disfavored and generally not acceptable for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa in the EdTech subscription sector. The Commercial Act requires a registered office at a specific, findable location for service of process, and the National Tax Service requires a real place of business for corporate tax registration, local VAT handling, business invoice issuance, and payroll. Korean banks implementing the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act and the KOFIU customer due diligence rules will normally inspect the lease, request utility bills, and may reject a corporate account if the registered address is only a virtual mailbox. A pure virtual office may be accepted only where there is a dedicated licensed desk, on-site reception service, written sublease, and actual place of management in Korea, but banks remain likely to treat this as a higher-risk shell indicator for an internet subscription business and require full commercial substance documentation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for tax and registry surveillance: (1) signboard at the registered address; (2) valid lease or ownership deed; (3) on-site callable representative; (4) IT equipment and workstation for the EdTech tutoring software; (5) accounting records and invoice registers; (6) statutory employment and subscription records; (7) physical workspace consistent with the declared business scope. Quantified risk of an unannounced on-site visit by the municipal tax office or the National Tax Service is approximately 15 percent in the first 18 months for a low-risk online EdTech LLC with no VAT refund activity, rising to 35-45 percent if the LLC files for export VAT zero-rating, claims excessive deductible expenses, or has no identifiable employee at the registered office. Registry authorities do not routinely conduct unannounced physical inspections but may mail a confirmation of address demand.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, including Articles 543 through 587 (limited liability company, Yuhan Hoesa), the incorporation registration rules of the Supreme Court, and the Framework Act on Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court Registry under the Supreme Court Administration of the Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation together with the Incorporation Registration Application filed with the competent Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Incorporation must state the capital amount, and all subscribed capital must be fully paid before the incorporation registration is filed. The paid-in capital must be deposited into a bank account opened in the name of the company and evidenced by a certificate of capital deposit. No blocked escrow account is required beyond the pre-registration restricted deposit period.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

RESOLUTION NO. 2025-BOD-001. The inaugural meeting of the Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company) was duly convened at the Company's registered office in the Republic of Korea at 10:00 a.m. on [date]. All initial directors were present in person or by proxy, and the meeting was duly constituted in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea.

WHEREAS the Company was organized as a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) to engage in interactive language education, automated tutoring software, subscription-based digital content, and related software services; WHEREAS the incorporators have subscribed for all initial shares, and the aggregate subscription price of KRW [amount] has been paid into the Company's subscription deposit account and is evidenced by the certificate of capital deposit issued by [bank]; WHEREAS the Company has selected its registered office in the Republic of Korea and has concluded a valid lease for that office; and WHEREAS the Company must establish banking relationships, statutory officers, and authorized filers to complete its incorporation registration and lawfully commence business.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

1. Capital Subscription and Issue. The Board ratifies and confirms the subscription and full payment of KRW [amount] in share capital. The Board approves the issuance of [number] ordinary shares to the initial members and directs the chief executive officer to file all capital subscription records with the competent Commercial Registry.

2. Banking Authorization. The Board designates [bank, branch, and account number] as the Company's primary bank account. The Board authorizes the chief executive officer, or in the case of absence the chief financial officer, to open, maintain, and operate corporate bank accounts in Korea, to receive settlement funds from Apple IAP, Google Play, and other payment channels, and to execute bank instructions, provided that transactions exceeding KRW [threshold] require dual signatures by two authorized directors or by the CEO and the auditor.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The Company's registered office shall be at [full address], Republic of Korea. The Board authorizes the CEO to pay the applicable registry fees, to submit the incorporation registration application, and to maintain the office as the legal seat for all statutory notices and service of process.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [name A] as representative director and chief executive officer of the Company, and appoints [name B] as statutory auditor (or, if applicable, as the second director with joint-representation authority), each to hold office until the next general meeting. The CEO is authorized to sign contracts, represent the Company before courts and tax authorities, and use the corporate seal.

5. Delegation, Filing, and Standing Authority. The CEO and the corporate secretary are authorized to execute and file the incorporation registration application, business registration application, tax registrations, corporate seal filings, and any ancillary declarations required by the Commercial Act, the National Tax Service, and the District Court Registry. All registrars, notaries, banks, and government offices are requested to accept the Company's execution of the attached forms.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this Resolution is effective immediately, that a certified extract be delivered to each bank and authority as evidence of authority, and that the original be placed in the corporate minute book. This Resolution was unanimously adopted by the Board on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public under the Korean Notary Association and the designated commercial bank in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator prepares the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, setting out the company name with Yuhan Hoesa status, the registered office location, the corporate purpose of interactive language education and automated tutoring software, the capital amount, share class, and the method of representation. The Articles must be signed or sealed by each initial member. The incorporator deposits the subscribed capital into a pre-registration deposit account at a licensed commercial bank and obtains a certificate of capital deposit. The notary certifies the legality of the Articles and verifies that the corporate purpose is lawful. No statutory minimum capital applies, but the full subscribed capital must be paid before the registration application can be filed.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identification of each initial member
Certificate of capital deposit issued by the Korean bank
Registered office lease contract or consent to use office
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the Articles because of a defective purpose clause, file corrected Articles with a revised lawful purpose and re-notarize in the same session. If the bank refuses the capital deposit due to source-of-funds or beneficial ownership questions, provide bank statements and a sworn certificate of beneficial ownership, or select another licensed commercial bank and obtain a fresh deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration Filing at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the Local District Court Registry having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization and capital payment, submit the incorporation registration application to the court registry in whose district the registered office is located. The application must use the prescribed commercial registration form and include the Articles of Incorporation, the certificate of capital deposit, proof of the registered office lease, and the written acceptance or consent of the initial directors and auditor. The registration officer verifies the company name, purpose, capital, payment, and representative authority. If the application is complete, the company is entered into the commercial register and an incorporation registration certificate is issued. Registration duty and local education surtax must be paid before or at the time of filing.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease and consent of lessor
Acceptance letters of initial directors and auditor
Power of attorney if submitted by a licensed filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or suspends the file, submit a formal written correction and supplementary evidence through the same registry within the statutory correction period. If the registration is rejected, apply for reconsideration before the district court or file a fresh application with cured defects and updated certified copies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Filing with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office, National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, and the Home Tax electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days from the commercial registration date, file the business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office. The application identifies the company as a VAT taxpayer, corporate income taxpayer, and withholding agent for employee and non-resident payments. The tax office verifies the registered office address and the existence of the corporation, after which it issues the business registration certificate. The company should also file for electronic tax invoice registration and VAT compliance. For pure digital EdTech subscription services, no separate industrial operating license is required; the business registration certificate is the core operating authorization for tax and commercial purposes.
required_dossiers: Lease contract for the registered office
Corporate seal certificate or seal imprint
Bank account proof or deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service questions the registered address or corporate substance, submit a corrected lease and a declaration explaining the digital business model. If the certificate is delayed, file an objection through the Home Tax tax-counsel channel and escalate to the district tax office supervision team. Provide proof of physical office access and representative presence if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Registration, Bank Account Activation and Statutory Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Court for corporate seal imprint, the selected licensed commercial bank, and Korean social insurance filing agencies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director must register the corporate seal with the court registry where the company is registered and obtain the corporate seal certificate. Thereafter, the company presents its incorporation registration certificate, business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, and representative director identification to activate its primary corporate bank account and electronic banking facilities. The company must also notify the tax office of its active bank account and, if employees are hired, register for social insurance at the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance through the joint electronic filing service. For a pure digital EdTech business, no industrial or physical manufacturing licenses are required.
required_dossiers: Social insurance employment register if hiring begins
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence because of foreign controllers or unusual settlement flows, submit notarized certificates of incumbency and a completed beneficial ownership declaration. If social insurance registration is queried, correct the employment register and file an adjustment through the joint electronic social insurance system within five business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital EdTech language learning software under ISIC 6201 and NAICS 611710 involves no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing establishment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no separate industrial operating license is required for subscription-based interactive education software under Korean law; the company holds only the general commercial and tax registrations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea does not require a permit for a pure software service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Full EIA Report, Initial EIA, or Environmental Registration is required because the digital EdTech service has no physical construction, discharge point, or pollutant-generating installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company has no wastewater discharge, VOC-emitting operations, or hazardous waste generation. If the company later adds physical server data centers or warehousing, it must pre-enter Stage 2 environmental review under the Clean Air Conservation Act, the Water Environment Preservation Act, and the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - the company operates no factory, warehouse, assembly line, or chemical facility requiring a Civil Defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or workplace chemical approval. The leased office must nonetheless remain in compliance with ordinary building fire prevention rules under the Korean Occupational Safety and Health Act, but no industrial Civil Defense clearance is triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with the official electronic fiscal portal known as the HomeTax System (Hometax)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) must obtain a business registration number from the NTS district tax office with jurisdiction over its Korean principal place of business, or if there is no Korean domestic place of business, from the Seoul Regional Tax Office or by appointing a tax representative in Korea. The foreign entity must file an application for business registration through the NTS HomeTax System or in person at the competent tax office, attaching its articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation or foreign company registration evidence, ownership and capital structure documentation, proof of the registered place of business or authorization of a domestic tax representative, and a power of attorney granting the tax representative the authority to accept Korean tax documents and filings. The NTS will then assign a 10-digit business registration number that functions as the Korean taxpayer identification number for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and withholding tax purposes. For a foreign non-resident entity with no fixed establishment, VAT registration obligations commence with the first provision of taxable supplies in Korea, and the appointed tax representative is jointly obliged to file and pay VAT on behalf of the foreign principal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the sense of a US-style check-the-box election. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is subject to entity-level corporation tax under the Corporation Tax Act and cannot elect pass-through or partnership treatment. A qualifying domestic holding company with wholly owned Korean subsidiaries may elect consolidated corporate income tax filing under the Corporation Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch or transparent entity election is available under Korean domestic law, but hybrid mismatch rules may recharacterize structures under the International Tax Adjustment Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold; any person making taxable supplies of goods or services in Korea is required to register for VAT regardless of turnover. Foreign non-resident suppliers of digital services to Korean customers are required to register for VAT through a tax representative beginning 1 July 2015, with no monetary threshold exemption. Domestic small businesses with annual gross receipts below KRW 80 million may be classified as simplified taxable persons, but this classification does not remove the obligation to register for VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses in Korea must issue an electronic tax invoice through the NTS HomeTax System, or through an NTS-approved EDI or ERP application integrated with the HomeTax interface, for every B2B supply of taxable goods or services. The electronic tax invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the date of issuance, and the NTS performs centralized real-time validation and matching of invoice data against VAT returns. There is no separate physical anti-fraud stamp requirement for ordinary digital or goods businesses; the mandatory electronic tax invoice transmission is the statutory anti-fraud control mechanism. Late or non-transmission of electronic tax invoices triggers additional taxes and penalties under the VAT Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment is available for goods that are exported from Korea under a valid export declaration filed with the Korea Customs Service. For digital and software-based language education services, including EdTech subscription services sold through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, zero rating may be claimed where the services are supplied to non-resident end customers, the digital service is treated as consumed outside Korea, payment is settled in foreign currency, and the service provider retains evidence of the foreign place of supply, foreign subscriber status, IP address or digital delivery logs, and app store or foreign exchange records. The Korean tax authority will deny zero rating if the taxpayer cannot substantiate that the goods physically left Korea or that the services were effectively supplied to a non-resident and consumed abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged with the Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Foreign exchange receipt confirmation issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Original supply contract or digital order records for digital services
IP address, device data, or digital delivery evidence demonstrating non-resident consumption of the EdTech service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export zero rating or VAT refund is claimed without the full statutory documentation, the NTS will disallow the zero rate, assess 10% output VAT on the underlying export supply, and impose additional VAT penalties and interest. Where the false export or false foreign exchange settlement is found to be fraudulent, the taxpayer is exposed to criminal liability and penalty taxes up to 40% of the underpaid tax, plus retroactive clawback of refunds paid. The statute of limitations for assessment is 5 years in ordinary cases and 10 years for fraudulent evasion. Failure to repatriate export proceeds in foreign currency within 180 days without a lawful extension granted by a Foreign Exchange Bank can also invalidate the zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Financial Supervisory Service under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized foreign exchange regime for current account transactions, but capital account operations remain subject to ex-ante and ex-post reporting through designated foreign exchange banks. The Korean won is not a fully offshore-deliverable currency; non-residents generally must execute conversion within Korea or through authorized offshore won market participants. For an EdTech subscription business, selling digital language-learning software into global markets gives rise to export proceeds that are considered invisible trade earnings and may be received in foreign currency. These receipts must be collected within 18 months from the date the export declaration is accepted, deposited into a corporate foreign currency account, and may be converted into KRW freely at market rates. Profit remittance as dividends is permissible after tax audits and foreign investment registration, but banks may require evidence that earnings were generated from licensed activity and that no outstanding transfer-pricing issues exist. Restrictions on capital repatriation are normally only procedural; however, any same-day round-tripping, over-invoicing, or use of unregistered overseas accounts will trigger BOK/FSS scrutiny. Overall convertibility is high for current receipts and low for speculative capital, with all FX transactions requiring traceability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds including digital services receipts must be collected within 18 months from the export declaration date. The full amount is subject to mandatory conversion into won or deposit into a foreign exchange bank account; maintaining foreign currency beyond the deadline requires prior approval from BOK or the delegated bank. For export settlement, the exporter must submit a settlement confirmation and invoice matching within 5 business days after receipt.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Overseas digital EMIs are not recognized as authorized deposit-taking institutions for Korean corporate entities. All cross-border settlement must be conducted through a licensed foreign exchange bank under Article 9 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Regulations prohibit unlicensed EMI accounts from functioning as corporate operating accounts for a Yuhan Hoesa, and fintech challengers without a Korean banking license cannot provide legally valid escrow or foreign currency collection services for this entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes, statutory directors must generally appear personally at a Korean bank branch for first-time corporate account opening. A consular notarized certificate of appointment and passport may be accepted only where the bank approves in advance as an alternative; however, biometric identity verification and FATF-compliant remote video opening are not uniformly accepted for foreign-owned LLCs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder secrecy: shareholder is a legal entity in a low-transparency jurisdiction and the UBO chain exceeds two tiers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate extract of each intermediary, share register and beneficial ownership declaration, ultimate UBO passport and address proof, notarized affidavit disclosing source of funds, and a written corporate ownership tree certified by a Korean attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance mismatch: EdTech subscription revenue is high but the company has no Korean employees or visible operations, creating shell risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employment contracts, monthly payroll remittances, R&D records, comprehensive software and curriculum evidence, customer subscription ledgers, Apple and Google settlement reports, and audited financial statements for the last two years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious cross-border volumetric spikes: inbound capital injections into the LLC do not match the stated business plan and are followed by rapid outbound disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete board resolutions, term sheets and subscription agreements, tax invoices, proof of domain and software licensing, bank statements showing traceability, and a notarized explanation of the commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse media, and PEP association in the principal shareholder or corporate officers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International passport copies, police certificate and criminal record clearance from the residence country, sanctions-list screening results from a reputable provider, negative media reports, and a comprehensive due diligence report authored by a FATF-recognized consultancy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a bank-designated foreign currency account in the name of the Korean entity. Prior to remittance, the foreign investor must file a foreign direct investment report with KOTRA or a designated bank and obtain a foreign investment number. Remittance instructions must include a purpose code representing direct investment and capital acquisition. After the funds are credited, the bank prepares a certificate of receipt of foreign capital, and the entity files the foreign investment registration with the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy. No trade invoice is required for equity, but a corresponding shareholder resolution and share issuance must be available.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of legitimate operational costs and dividend remittance is done through SWIFT MT103, MT202, or MT232 for vendor payments; where the Korean entity imports physical educational hardware, a commercial letter of credit issued by a Korean bank with a documentary collection alternative is acceptable. Each wire must be supported by contract, invoice, customs or VAT letter, and carry an approved FX purpose code. For Apple and Google in-app payment rails, settlement flows from foreign app stores are remitted as invisible trade receipts under the appropriate purpose code, and the company must ensure the stored foreign exchange is booked as export revenue.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable currency forward contracts with licensed Korean banks based on underlying trade receivables and payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for non-resident counterparties with a valid underlying trade exposure and central bank approval
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term convertibility hedging, limited to actual loan principal and interest projections

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Equity Holders' Meeting and Financial Statement Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; if registered changes arise, competent Local Registration Court / Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene and approve the financial statements may expose the company to Commercial Act administrative penalties, deemed corporate income determinations, and, for chronically dormant companies, registration deletion by the local court after repeated non-filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Final Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; next business day if the deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax; understatement surcharge of 10%; fraudulent understatement or concealment surcharge of 40%; late-payment interest of 0.022% per day; persistent delinquency leads to enforced collection, asset seizure, and administrative closure of the business registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the end of the first six months of the fiscal year; for a January 1 - December 31 fiscal year, no later than August 31; applies if the previous year's corporate income tax liability exceeded KRW 5,000,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficiency triggers interim-tax surcharge plus late-payment interest of 0.022% per day; failure to pay can accelerate full-year collection and seizure of corporate bank accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government tax authority (WeTax; e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government for a Seoul-registered company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge under the Local Tax Collection Act, generally 3% of the unpaid local tax plus 0.022% per day interest; prolonged non-payment results in local government enforced collection proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 25 for the January 1 - March 31 VAT tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing VAT surcharge of 20% of the payable tax; false or excessive input tax claims attract 40% surcharge; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% applies until payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 for the January 1 - June 30 VAT tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing VAT surcharge of 20% of the payable tax; understatement and false refund surcharges up to 40%; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% applies until payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: October 25 for the July 1 - September 30 VAT tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing VAT surcharge of 20% of the payable tax; false or excessive input tax claims attract 40% surcharge; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% applies until payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following year for the July 1 - December 31 VAT tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing VAT surcharge of 20% of the payable tax; understatement and false refund surcharges up to 40%; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% applies until payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Annual Salary and Wage Withholding Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) / competent district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual consolidated salary withholding report due by March 10 of the following year; monthly withholding payments due by the 10th day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file withholding statements attracts penalty surcharges under the Income Tax Act, including up to 1% of the unreported amount and daily late-payment interest; employers failing to withhold may be liable for the uncollected employee tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART e-filing system; audited financial statements also filed with National Tax Service with the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end for audited entities required to file under the external audit regime; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or file the audit report can trigger administrative fines and criminal penalties under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, reputational sanctions by FSS, and tax-office closure if underlying tax filings also remain delinquent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Business Status Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA Foreign Investment Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of each fiscal year if the Yuhan Hoesa maintains foreign-invested company status; shareholding transfers must be reported within 30 days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report can result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 2,000,000, loss of foreign-invested company designation, cancellation of tax and customs incentives, and adverse enforcement by MOTIE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Corporate Minute Book Validation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No public filing required; internal corporate secretarial control, subject to production on order of court, NTS, or Financial Supervisory Service in an audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the Equity Holders' Meeting; promptly after any share transfer, appointment, or change in registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or false registers can create Commercial Act liability for officers, voidable meeting resolutions, and monetary sanctions; sustained absence of valid corporate records may be used by authorities to presume dormancy and initiate registration deletion

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national corporate income tax on taxable income above KRW 20 billion plus 10% local income tax surtax, yielding a 23.1% top effective headline rate; lower brackets are 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million and 19% on taxable income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free-economic-zone foreign-invested high-tech enterprises are eligible for up to 100% national corporate tax exemption for 5 years and 50% exemption for the following 2 years; venture SMEs and new growth industry companies may claim statutory tax reductions; qualifying R&D expenditures and job creation tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act can meaningfully reduce the effective tax rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Tax Base and Tax Amount (CIT Form, filed through the HomeTax electronic filing system under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act), including the Foreign Related-Party Transaction Disclosure Schedule and shareholder/beneficial ownership schedule for Korean LLCs with non-resident ownership.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within 3 months after the end of the Korean LLC fiscal year; if the Korean taxpayer files with the assistance of a certified tax accountant or obtains independent review, the filing period may be extended by one month, making the effective deadline 4 months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity Identification and Non-Resident Control Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity name, corporate registration number, head office address, representative director information, and declaration of the place of effective management. The Korean Yuhan Hoesa must identify non-resident shareholders, their tax residence, ownership percentage, and any foreign individual or legal person exercising practical control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder's full legal name, nationality, address, and tax residence code must be reported exactly as it appears on the Tax Residency Certificate. If the beneficial owner is a foreign EdTech platform operator, attach the organizational chart, board meeting minutes, and registered agency agreement proving that the Korean LLC is not a mere nominee; failure to do so invites treaty disallowance and piercing of the corporate veil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Gross Income and Worldwide Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross revenue from interactive language education and automated tutoring software subscriptions, including Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, corporate sales, licensing, and incidental advertising. The Korean LLC is taxed on worldwide income because it is domestically incorporated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source revenue must still be included in gross income; it is not outside the Korean tax base merely because the payment is routed to a non-resident payment processor or marketed through a foreign affiliate. Gross revenue understatement through undisclosed app-store settlement accounts is a fatal red flag that triggers the full audit and criminal examination protocol.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 22 - Related-Party Transactions and Arm's-Length Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed disclosure of all transactions with foreign related parties, including royalty payments, management fees, cloud hosting fees, marketing payments, and app-store distribution agreements. The taxpayer must attach the transfer pricing schedule and indicate whether any transfer pricing adjustment increases taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident related party cannot be used to price Korean EdTech intangible services at artificial levels. If the Korean LLC overpays an offshore affiliate for software licenses or management support, the National Tax Service will adjust the transaction, disallow the deduction, and reclassify the excess payment as a non-resident dividend subject to withholding tax. Maintain the Local File and Master File showing functional analysis, risk assumption, CUP or TNMM benchmarking, and Core Income-Generating Activities performed by the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 11 - Exemptions and Reduced Tax Rate Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule for statutory exemptions and reductions, including venture SME tax reductions, job creation credits, R&D credits, special foreign-investment zone benefits, and local income tax surtax exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC must verify that non-resident ownership does not disqualify any SME or venture-company incentive. Dividends or profit withdrawals to non-resident shareholders are not deductible expenses and cannot be relabeled as consulting fees, technology fees, or interest in order to shift income; expenses must satisfy economic substance requirements and arm's-length conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign income taxes paid or accrued on foreign-source income. The schedule calculates the credit limitation as Korean corporate income tax attributable to foreign-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only genuinely paid or accrued foreign income taxes may be credited, and supporting foreign tax assessment or receipt evidence must be attached. The credit cannot exceed the Korean tax limitation, and no credit is available for taxes attributable to a non-resident shareholder or foreign affiliate rather than to the Korean taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 44 - Non-Resident Interest, Dividend, and Royalty Withholding Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of domestic withholding obligations on payments made to non-residents, including dividends, interest, royalties, and certain service fees; the schedule reflects the 20% national withholding tax and 10% local surtax on national withholding, producing a 22% combined statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a tax treaty reduction is claimed, attach the withholding tax exemption/reduction application, the foreign Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence that the non-resident recipient does not have a permanent establishment in Korea. A Korean distributor or marketing agent cannot be deemed the beneficial owner solely because the app-store contract names such distributor; substance determines entitlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file is subject to a 20% penalty on the unpaid tax; understatement attracts 10%; fraudulent understatement attracts 40%; unpaid tax also accrues a monthly delinquency charge of 0.75% up to a maximum of 36 months. Failure to disclose foreign related-party transactions or to produce transfer pricing documentation on demand triggers an additional transfer pricing penalty under the International Tax Coordination Act, and willful evasion is referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% for outbound dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, composed of 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national withholding amount; treaty may reduce the rate if the foreign shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must file the Korean withholding tax exemption/reduction application before or at the time of the remittance and the payer must transmit the application to the relevant district tax office. The application package must include the Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty jurisdiction for the fiscal year in which the income is paid, a beneficial ownership declaration identifying the ultimate recipient as not a conduit, proof that the recipient has no permanent establishment in Korea, and copies of the underlying dividend, interest, or royalty contracts. If the reduced rate is not applied before the payment date, recovery of excess withholding is pursued through a claim for refund under the Framework Act on National Taxes and supporting treaty documents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalties paid to non-resident corporations are each subject to a 22% combined domestic withholding rate (20% national plus 10% local surtax); most Korean bilateral treaties reduce interest and royalties to 10% or 15% where the beneficial owner qualifies and the activity is not effectively connected with a Korean permanent establishment. Contractual gross-up clauses shifting the Korean withholding tax to the Korean payer are non-deductible expenses for corporate tax purposes and are treated as additional dividends or compensation subject to transfer pricing review.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is statutorily triggered when cross-border intercompany transactions exceed KRW 10 billion in a fiscal year, and the Master File is required when the Korean entity belongs to an MNE group with annual consolidated revenue of at least KRW 100 billion; separate transfer pricing disclosure forms must be filed through the annual corporate income tax return for foreign related-party transactions exceeding KRW 100 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations but enforces substance-over-form principles, beneficial ownership tests, and CFC rules. The Korean Yuhan Hoesa must demonstrate real employees, board decisions, contracts, financial accounts, and Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea, covering EdTech content maintenance, user onboarding, subscription pricing, Apple/Google settlement, technical support, and commercial risk. A shell Korean LLC funding a low-tax foreign affiliate and claiming treaty benefits or CFC exemptions without local operating substance will be recharacterized by the Korean tax authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Underreporting of Digital Subscription Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC routes Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds to a non-resident payment account controlled by an undisclosed foreign beneficial owner, reports only the net remittance as revenue, and records the difference as marketing expense paid to a shell company. The corporate income tax return omits true gross revenue and non-resident ownership details.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act prescribes imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to ten times the evaded corporate income tax, together with a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty and monthly delinquency surcharges up to 36 months on the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who commingle corporate revenue with personal or foreign affiliate accounts or sign false settlement certificates can be personally assessed for the evaded tax and penalties under piercing-of-the-corporate-veil principles; personal assets may be seized, the directors may be blacklisted as chronic delinquents, and departure restrictions may be imposed while the criminal tax investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse / Artificial Profit Siphoning Through Low-Substance Foreign Affiliates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa pays 90% of its subscription revenue as royalties, management fees, and app-store distribution fees to a Hong Kong or other low-tax intermediary that employs no developers, owns no validated EdTech intellectual property, performs no active board or risk functions, and provides no evidence of Core Income-Generating Activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 5 of the International Tax Coordination Act authorizes the National Tax Service to adjust the intercompany price to arm's length; the excess royalty or fee is nondeductible, additional transfer pricing penalties of 10% may apply, and the disallowed amount can be recharacterized as a constructive dividend or royalty subject to 22% withholding under the Corporate Income Tax Act and the Local Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute and approve artificial intercompany agreements may be jointly and severally liable for the tax and penalties if the Korean corporation is insolvent; deliberate false documentation subjects them to criminal liability, asset attachment, travel bans, and recovery actions against personal property in the hands of the foreign affiliate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Wilful Withholding Tax Evasion and Fraudulent DTA Treaty Relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC distributes profits to a non-resident parent without deducting the 22% dividend withholding tax and attempts treaty relief under a favorable DTA by submitting a fraudulent or acquired Tax Residency Certificate while the true place of effective management or economic ownership remains in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agents are liable under Article 73 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and Article 103-12 of the Local Tax Act for the unpaid 22% tax and penalties; fraudulent treaty claims are penalized as tax evasion under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and the assessment period is extended to 10 years for dishonest or intentional concealment under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize an un-withheld dividend or knowingly submit a false Tax Residency Certificate may be criminally prosecuted, deprived of departure rights, subjected to court-authorized asset freezing, and held personally liable for the withholding liability when the corporate entity is only an emptying shell used to avoid Korean tax.
